Author: Dipankar Datta Bench: Dipankar Datta
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL Nos. OF 2025  (@ SLP (Crl.) No.9753-9754/2024)
 HARMEET SINGH APPELLANT  VERSUS  SURPRIYA RESPONDENT  ORDER 1.
Leave granted.

2. In course of hearing of these appeals, the appellant-husband (Mr. Harmeet Singh) and the respondent-wife (Ms. Surpriya) were referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre for exploring a settlement through the process of mediation.
3. The process of mediation has produced positive results.
The Mediator has sent a report that the parties have agreed to resolve the inter se disputes and differences amicably.
It has also been decided by them to apply before this Court seeking dissolution of their marriage by mutual consent under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
4. The parties have jointly filed an application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, being I.A. No.187788/2025, in view of such settlement.

The prayers in the application under Article 142 read as follows:
a. Allow the Application and Grant Decree for Divorce by Mutual Consent.
b. Quash all the Criminal/Civil Cases filed by the Parties against each other and family members in terms of the Settlement Agreement (Annexure A-1); and c. Issue direction to correct the name of the respondent as Surpriya in the judgment/order/decree passed by this Honble Court; and d. Pass such further Harmeet Singh vs Supriya on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110373377/
1 order/orders as this Honble Court may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.
5. Settlement agreement agreed by and between the parties inter alia reads as follows:
A. That the Parties have agreed that the Petitioner-husband will pay to the Respondent-wife a total sum of Rs.18,00,000/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs Only)
towards full and final settlement of all her claims towards her permanent alimony,
Stridhan, maintenance (past, present, future) and any other claim whatsoever.

The mode of payment is as under: -
(i) The Petitioner-husband shall pay first installment of an amount of Rs.6,00,000/-
(Rupees Six Lakhs Only) in favour of the Respondent wife by way of RTGS/Online on or before 01.01.2025.
(ii) The petitioner-husband shall pay Second installment an amount of Rs.6,00,000/-
(Rupees Six Lakhs Only) in favour of the Respondent wife by way of RTGS/Online on or before 01.02.2025.
(iii) The Petitioner-husband shall pay Third/Last installment an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Only) in favour of the Respondent wife by way of RTGS/Online on or before 01.03.2025

The Account details of the Respondent-wife is as under:-
Account Bearing No.0359000101037216 in the Name of (Supriya Heera) IFSC Code:-PUNB0035900 Punjab National Bank, Nangal Branch, Dist. Roopnagar,
Punjab 6.
During the course of the dispute, the parties filed various cases against each other.

List of cases pending by and between the parties before various courts is as under:
(i) The Petitioner has filed divorce petition DMC No.887 of 2023 pending before Jalandhar, District Court Jalandhar,
(ii) The Petitioner Lodged FIR quashing CRM M No.15053 of 2021 pending before Punjab and Haryana High Court, at Chandigarh,
(iii) The Petitioner has filed Perjury CRM M No.40766 of 2021 pending before Punjab and Haryana, at Chandigarh,
(iv) The Petitioner-husband has filed Transfer Application CRM M No.47078 of 2023 pending before Punjab and Haryana High Court, at Chandigarh,

sentences.text: (v) The Respondent wife had filed a Transfer Application bearing T.A. No.748 of 2023 which was dismissed by the Punjab and Haryana High Court vide judgment and order dated 04.12.2024.

(vi) The Respondent wife has filed a Petition under Section 125 Cr.P.C. for maintenance bearing MNT No.125/31/2022 before the Family Court, Nangal,
Punjab,
(vii) The Respondent wife has filed a Petition under the D.V. Act bearing COMA/1/2023 before the Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Nangal, District Roopnagar, Punjab,
(viii) The Respondent wife has got an FIR registered bearing FIR No.25 of 2021 P.S.
Nangal, District Roopnagar, Punjab under Sections 498A, 420, 406 and 506 of erstwhile Indian Penal Code.
7.
The appellant-husband and the respondent-wife have joined the proceedings virtually.

Responding to our query, they have separately submitted that the settlement has been arrived at by them voluntarily and there has been no undue influence or pressure from any side, that they are agreeable to have their marriage dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent and that all proceedings instituted by either of them against the other may be quashed.
8. The parties having amicably resolved the inter se disputes and differences, the terms of settlement which are contained in the joint application shall form part of this order.

9. Accordingly, in exercise of power conferred on us by Article 142 of the Constitution of India, we dissolve the marriage between the parties by mutual consent by granting an order in terms of prayers (a), (b) & (c) of the joint application.
Decree be drawn up, accordingly.
10. As a result of this order, nothing survives for decision on these appeals.
The appeals stand disposed of together with I.A. No.187788/2025.
11. The relevant courts/police stations shall mark closure of the cases/proceedings/complaints that are pending/lodged before it, once this order is received.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
13. We appreciate the efforts of the mediator in assisting the parties to resolve their disputes amicably.
New Delhi;
September 26, 2025.
